[LGRA.9.8.11] **The built-in set is closed** ([LCYC.1.2]): every
callable name in an expression is a built-in of this section. The compiler must reject a call to any other
name with `DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`, naming the admitted set.

A series aggregation read in call form ([LSER.16.1]) is a built-in for this
purpose. An aggregation the bound series does not declare is [LSER.6.9.4]'s
refusal, and a name that is no aggregation is refused here.

The two functions of a `unit formula` ([LUNI.4.5]) are callable too, in a file
that declares the formula or imports it ([LIMP.7.7]), outside a formula's body. The compiler **must**
resolve such a call to the formula, check its argument against the function's
parameter unit as any unit-typed operand is checked, and evaluate it as the
function's expression at the call site. A formula is declared only as a
conversion between two units, and its body is one expression over its one
parameter ([LUNI.4.5]).

Every call in a formula's body is to a built-in. The compiler **must** reject a
call there to a formula's function, the formula's own included, with
`DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`, at the formula's declaration, whether or not
anything calls the formula.
